summary: We developed a prototype of a Virtual Reality game that would allow someone to explore Earth Information Centre data visualizations through an Earth Jukebox. In the VR game, users would blast off in a rocket into space, then they would explore the moon and also look off into the horizon and see Earth. When they engage with the Earth, it turns into a Jukebox and they can watch data visualizations of earth science events like hurricanes, global sea temperature rise. We created the sounds to go with the data visualizations to enhance the experience.
details:
It's a VR experience that brings to life NASA Earth Information Centre visualizations so that people can not only watch the data visualizations of earth science phenomenon but also listen to them. We used the music-AI, called SONILO to create the sound for Track 1 Map of human-made carbon dioxide emissions. It made a cool song that matched the visualizations but we decided that we wanted more control over the soundscapes and so for Track 2 Global Sea Temperature we used a Chrome Music Lab application called Spectograph to experiment with sounds that worked with the slow circulating currents in the ocean. We liked the human-creative process and the outcome much better. So we would not automate the sounds through AI. The third track, worked with Hurricane Season data from 2022 and we used Chrome Music Lab and the application, Songmaker, to visually create the song and then modified the visual blocks until we felt it matched the data visualization.

We think this VR game will be an immersive experience for people to learn about earth science while also experiencing thoughtfully-created soundscapes and also having fun while exploring the moon and the Earth jukebox.

To compile the data visualizations with the sounds, we used IMOVIE and then uploaded videos to Youtube.
